# Autonomy

This policy describes contribution boundaries; explicit session authorization remains
valid and can settle choices within its scope. Repository policy cannot grant authority
over a consumer repository, a global agent installation or external publication.

## May do without a new question

Read the kit and relevant consumer source, inspect local development specimens, author
intent/design/decision records, implement and verify a scoped requested improvement.
Choose routine architecture details consistent with accepted decisions. Prepare a
reviewable migration/release candidate. Record local evidence and declared divergences.
A consumer's product intent always governs its domain and user experience.

## Ask only at an unresolved authority boundary

Publishing/tagging/releases, deploying, changing global agent configuration, real user
data or signing credentials, materially destructive operations, and cross-project writes
need authorization for that actual action. Existing session authorization counts; do not
ask again merely because the action appears in this list. Prepare all safe reviewable
work first. Read-only fleet investigation is not a cross-project mutation.

## Never

Claim a host loaded instructions because files exist. Call a skipped check passed.
Hide a runtime limitation, invent a license entitlement, publish paid source without
rights, bypass a gate, silently change a consumer's framework, overwrite unrelated work,
force-push main, or claim product excellence solely from tests or screenshots.

## Branch model

The current repository works on main; this document does not invent an integration
branch or authorize an unsolicited push. For a requested implementation, use the
current branch when safe or an isolated worktree for conflicting concurrent work.
Commit/push according to the active task's authorization, one reviewable unit at a time;
commits carry an honest Verified: line. Preserve unrelated local changes and stashes.
Separate agents may share a checkout only with explicit non-overlapping file ownership.

## Evidence and execution

Local checks and task fixtures should use synthetic data. Host configuration and policy
distribution are explicit reviewed changes. Runtime apps do not need MCP or a sibling
checkout to operate. Instructions guide judgment; actual gates must prove invocation
and refusal of a seeded violation before being described as enforced.
